alt.en: A carved stone tablet set into a wall of grey flints. In Gothic lettering it reads "This Church dates from 1689. Secular buildings on this site 1721 adapted for worship. First Chapel erected 1764. Second Chapel erected 1836." The edge of a blue-grey door frame shows at the right.
alt.es: Una lápida de piedra tallada, encastrada en un muro de pedernal gris. En letra gótica dice "This Church dates from 1689. Secular buildings on this site 1721 adapted for worship. First Chapel erected 1764. Second Chapel erected 1836." A la derecha se ve el borde de un marco de puerta gris azulado.

caption.en: A stone on today's St Andrew's Street Baptist Church in Cambridge, the church Robinson served from 1759, records its first chapel, built in 1764, the year his congregation, grown under his preaching, opened a new meeting-house in place of the ruinous old one, once a barn.
caption.es: Una lápida de la actual iglesia bautista de St Andrew's Street, en Cambridge, la iglesia a la que Robinson sirvió desde 1759, recuerda su primera capilla, construida en 1764, el año en que su congregación, que había crecido con su predicación, abrió un nuevo local de reunión en lugar del viejo y ruinoso, antes un granero.

source: St Andrew's Street Baptist Church, St Andrew's Street, Cambridge (October 2025) (Foundation Stone) (1), photograph, 10 October 2025

alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of a printed book page headed "[ 73 ]" and "HYMN LXXI.", with three numbered stanzas beginning "COME thou Fount of ev'ry Blessing!" in old type with the long s. Small signs (an asterisk, double bar, dagger, double dagger and section mark) in the lines match Bible references at the foot: "Heb. i. 7. Heb xii. 18-25. Mal. iii. 6. James i. 17. 1 Sam. vii. 12. 2 Cor. i. 22. Eph. i. 13." Text from the facing page shows faintly through the paper. There is no music.
alt.es: Imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de una página impresa con el encabezado "[ 73 ]" y "HYMN LXXI.", con tres estrofas numeradas que empiezan "COME thou Fount of ev'ry Blessing!" en tipografía antigua con la s larga. Unos signos pequeños (asterisco, doble barra, cruz, doble cruz y signo de párrafo) en los versos remiten a las citas bíblicas al pie: "Heb. i. 7. Heb xii. 18-25. Mal. iii. 6. James i. 17. 1 Sam. vii. 12. 2 Cor. i. 22. Eph. i. 13." El texto de la página de enfrente se transparenta un poco. No hay música.

caption.en: Hymn LXXI in Martin Madan's Collection of Psalms and Hymns (London, 1760), p. 73: the three-stanza text most books have followed since, with Madan's signs keyed to Bible references at the foot of the page.
caption.es: El himno LXXI de la Collection of Psalms and Hymns de Martin Madan (Londres, 1760), p. 73: el texto de tres estrofas que desde entonces siguen la mayoría de los libros, con los signos de Madan que remiten a citas bíblicas al pie de la página.

source: A collection of psalms and hymns, extracted from various authors, and published by the Reverend Mr. Madan (London, 1760), Hymn LXXI, p. 73
library: Internet Archive, Eighteenth Century collection (from microfilm)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1760; editor Martin Madan died 1790, author Robert Robinson died 1790. Faithful microfilm scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: A wide, yellowed title page inside a printed ornamental border, reading "Wyeth's Repository of Sacred Music. Part Second. Original and selected from the most eminent and approved authors in that science, for the use of Christian churches, singing-schools & private societies. Together with a copious and plain introduction to the grounds of music, and rules for learners. By John Wyeth." At the foot: "Printed (typographically) at Harrisburgh, Penn. by John Wyeth, Printer and Bookseller, and sold by him, and by Mathew Carey, Market-street, Philadelphia" and "1813."
alt.es: Una portada ancha y amarillenta, dentro de una orla impresa, con el texto "Wyeth's Repository of Sacred Music. Part Second. Original and selected from the most eminent and approved authors in that science, for the use of Christian churches, singing-schools & private societies. Together with a copious and plain introduction to the grounds of music, and rules for learners. By John Wyeth." Al pie: "Printed (typographically) at Harrisburgh, Penn. by John Wyeth, Printer and Bookseller, and sold by him, and by Mathew Carey, Market-street, Philadelphia" y "1813."

caption.en: The title page of Wyeth's Repository of Sacred Music, Part Second (Harrisburg, 1813), the book that holds the earliest known printing of NETTLETON, there called HALLELUJAH.
caption.es: La portada de Wyeth's Repository of Sacred Music, Part Second (Harrisburg, 1813), el libro con la primera impresión conocida de NETTLETON, que allí se llama HALLELUJAH.

source: Wyeth's repository of sacred music. Part second, by John Wyeth (Harrisburgh, Penn.: John Wyeth, 1813), title page

alt.en: A cream-coloured page of printed music headed "Worship", then "19 NETTLETON 8s. 7s. D." with "John Wyeth" at the right. Four systems of two staves in 3/4 with three flats carry verse 1, from "Come, thou Fount of every blessing" to "Mount of thy redeeming love. A-men." Verses 2 and 3 are printed below in two columns, signed "Robert Robinson".
alt.es: Una página de música impresa, color crema, con el encabezado "Worship" y después "19 NETTLETON 8s. 7s. D.", con "John Wyeth" a la derecha. Cuatro sistemas de dos pentagramas a 3/4, con tres bemoles, llevan la estrofa 1, desde "Come, thou Fount of every blessing" hasta "Mount of thy redeeming love. A-men." Las estrofas 2 y 3 van debajo en dos columnas, firmadas "Robert Robinson".

caption.en: NETTLETON as No. 19 of The Methodist Hymnal (New York, 1905), p. 14, the four parts our arrangement reads, credited there to John Wyeth, whose book of 1813 is its earliest known printing.
caption.es: NETTLETON en el n.º 19 de The Methodist Hymnal (Nueva York, 1905), p. 14, las cuatro voces que lee nuestro arreglo, atribuida allí a John Wyeth, cuyo libro de 1813 es su primera impresión conocida.

source: The Methodist hymnal: official hymnal of the Methodist Episcopal Church and the Methodist Episcopal Church, South (New York: Eaton & Mains; Cincinnati: Jennings & Graham, 1905), No. 19, "Nettleton", p. 14
